_README: Feed-driven sources for the research monitor (AI/data-center market risk, grid buildout, ag/climate, forestry, inequality, IPCC). Ported from the Claude-app scheduled tasks after their unattended WebFetch calls were getting auto-denied — these are plain RSS pulls instead, so there's no permission gate to hit. type 'rss' is parsed as generic RSS/Atom via research_pull.py. Curation (cutting low-value sources, adding new ones) happens in the Tuesday session, not here automatically. Stage 1 (weekly) verified 2026-09-12; Stage 2 (monthly-cadence additions) verified 2026-09-12 the same way — live curl against each feed URL before trusting it — see individual 'notes' fields. Quarterly/annual sources are NOT in this file at all — those are calendar-triggered via research_calendar.json + main.py's collect_calendar(), same mechanism as calendar.json's personal/seasonal events, not pulled daily. research_data/<id>.json's freshness is checked cadence-aware by research_validate.py, keyed off each source's 'cadence' field below.

sources.label: Epoch AI — Gradient Updates & Data Insights
sources.notes: Quantitative AI-trends shop. Highest-signal bull-case data source. KNOWN ISSUE (confirmed 2026-09-15): the GitHub Actions cron has 403'd on this feed for at least 2 consecutive daily runs (9/13, 9/14) despite the retry-with-backoff added 9/12 — same fetch succeeds instantly from a normal residential/office IP. This reads as the same Substack/Cloudflare-vs-GitHub-Actions-runner-IP wall already documented as a dead end in CLAUDE.md for a different feature, not a transient blip retrying harder will fix. Workaround: the Tuesday interactive session has normal network access and can fetch this feed directly when the cron's copy is stale/errored — do that rather than sinking more time into the cron side. Separately, checked 2026-09-12 whether 'The Epoch Brief' (Epoch's monthly digest, per the original source plan's Stage 2) needs a separate integration: it does not — it publishes into this same Substack feed with a distinct, greppable title pattern ('The Epoch Brief - <date>', confirmed live: Sep 12, Jul 31, Jul 8, Jun 26, Jun 12, May 22, May 15 2026 — actually closer to twice-monthly than strictly monthly). The weekly pull already captures every Brief issue; no new source needed. The Tuesday session can just look for that title prefix when synthesizing.

sources.label: SemiAnalysis
sources.notes: Semiconductor/data-center supply chain analysis. Free tier only — paid Core Research posts may appear in the feed but are gated; skip if content is truncated.

sources.label: farmdoc daily
sources.notes: Publishes daily — treat as a weekly digest and summarize the 1-3 most notable posts from the past week, not every item.

sources.label: US Drought Monitor — Indiana
sources.notes: No RSS. Uses the USDM data service JSON API directly (structured data, not scraped HTML) — updates every Thursday. aoi param needs Indiana's FIPS code (18), not 'IN' — confirmed 2026-09-12.

sources.label: Indiana DNR Division of Water — Monthly Water Resource Summary
sources.notes: Added 2026-09-29. Fills the water/groundwater gap. Written by the state Division of Water for water managers: precipitation and SPI classes, Drought Monitor status, streamflow vs normal, and a groundwater classification for the nine observation wells ('above normal', 'near normal', 'well below normal') - the Division's own categories, not raw well readings. Normal months are stated plainly (August 2026: 'near normal for four of nine wells'). Keyless, static server-rendered HTML; no RSS. Verified 2026-09-29 by live fetch: the page shows only the latest month under an h2 like 'August 2026', h3 sections beneath, so fetch_items() emits one item per pull dated month-end with link #month-YYYY-MM and the history ledger builds the series (older months are not on the page). Gotchas: the page has no publish date, only the month heading, and the summary often lands in the first week or two of the following month, so a monthly cadence with the 10-day freshness window is right; scraper returns [] (status empty, flagged by validate) if the h2/h3 layout changes; not yet confirmed that the GitHub Actions runner IP can reach in.gov (worked from a residential IP). Rejected alternatives: USGS WaterWatch and Groundwater Watch are decommissioned (WaterWatch pages now redirect to a decommission blog post); USGS state pages and statistics APIs are keyed or raw. Weekly Moisture Report (PDFs at in.gov/drought/files/drought-water-soil-conditions-MMDDYYYY.pdf, irregular dates) is an email subscription and not scraped.

sources.label: USDA NASS Crop Progress — Indiana
sources.notes: Verified 2026-09-12 against live data once NASS_API_KEY was added. Two real bugs surfaced and were fixed during verification: a title/summary date mismatch, and a label collision where CORN's grain vs. silage harvest sub-series (distinguished by util_practice_desc, not class_desc) both rendered as generic 'Harvested: N%'. Only meaningful April-November; returns empty (not an error) off-season.

sources.label: interconnection.fyi — Indiana data-center tracker
sources.notes: No RSS/API, but the page's __NEXT_DATA__ script tag embeds the full project list as JSON — read that directly instead of scraping rendered HTML. This is a live snapshot, not a chronological feed, so fetch_items() emits one dated summary (counts by status/county) per pull rather than per-project items; the history ledger is what lets the Tuesday session compare week over week.

sources.label: interconnection.fyi — US data-center tracker (national benchmark for Indiana)
sources.notes: Added 2026-09-29 as the national benchmark beside interconnection_fyi. Verified live 2026-09-29: the landing page (/data-center) embeds __NEXT_DATA__ with statusCounts, totalProjectCount and statesWithProjects (48 codes, including Canadian AB and ON) but NO per-state counts, so the scraper also fetches the 48 state pages (~0.3s each, TX ~0.9MB) and computes counts by status, top states by pipeline (Proposed + Construction), and Indiana's rank/share on that same basis (2026-09-29: IN rank 4 of 46 US states on pipeline, 39 of 972 = 4.0%; 4 of 2,435 operational, rank 32). GOTCHA: the landing headline (12,538 records, 4,862 of them status Unknown) is ~3x the sum of the state pages (3,922 projects) and the status splits differ; not reconcilable from the pages, so the summary keeps the two bases apart and ranks only on state pages (same basis as the Indiana scrape). Raw counts are noisy (TX lists entries like '(100% VACANT)TEXAS UTILITIES'; capacityRange is null for most), so read ranks and shares as rough, and trends in the ledger over levels. Slow-moving series: an unchanged snapshot from week to week is the source doing its job, not a stale scraper. Site is GridTracker's tracker (secondary aggregation of public records, not a research shop); it is judged as a benchmark for Indiana, not as an expert synthesis in its own right. Emits one date-fragmented item per pull into research_data/history/interconnection_fyi_national.jsonl.

sources.label: Epoch AI — AI data centers hub (global benchmark)
sources.notes: Added 2026-09-29 as the global benchmark. Expert-built (satellite imagery, permits, filings) estimates of power, H100-equivalents and cost for the world's largest AI data centers; CC-BY (credit Epoch AI). Keyless CSV at https://epoch.ai/data/data_centers/data_centers.csv (found on the hub page's Downloads list; the timelines CSV alongside it holds dated construction trajectories, not used yet). Verified live 2026-09-29: 93 sites, 13.5 GW current power (matches the hub headline '13.5 GW IT power'; the CSV column is labelled 'Current power (MW)'), 14.0M H100-eq, US 88% of covered power, China 5%, Malaysia 4%; Indiana 3 sites (New Carlisle 910 MW, Jeffersonville 178 MW, Fort Wayne 0 MW) = 8.1% of the covered total. Indiana sites are matched by 'IN'/'Indiana' in the Address column (a few US rows have blank addresses, so the count could undercount). GOTCHA: coverage is Epoch's selection (hub says ~44% of global AI compute, lower bar internationally), so shares are of the covered set, not world capacity; the summary says so. The dataset is updated roughly weekly to monthly, and the scraper reads 'Updated <date>' from the hub page (best-effort) so a repeated vintage is visible: an unchanged dataset is normal for a slow-moving series, not a failure. Epoch's Substack feed is a separate source (epoch_ai). Annual global energy benchmarks (IEA) are in research_calendar.json, not here.

sources.label: Federal Reserve Beige Book - Chicago District and national
sources.notes: Added 2026-09-29. Recession early warning, expert-synthesized: Reserve Bank staff summarize anecdotes from business contacts, in plain words, and say so when little changed (Chicago, Sep 2 2026: consumer spending and construction 'flat on balance', nonbusiness contacts 'no change'; national: 'two Districts reported no change'). Released 8 times a year, about two weeks before each FOMC meeting. No RSS (checked the Fed's feeds.htm list 2026-09-29: none for the Beige Book). Edition URLs are stable: beigebookYYYYMM-summary.htm and -chicago.htm, YYYYMM = end of the reporting period (the Sep 2 2026 release is 202608); the landing page links every edition of the year and the scraper takes the highest. One item per edition, linked to that edition's URL so the history ledger accumulates one entry per release; item date is the summary page's 'Last Update' stamp (= release date unless the Fed revises the page). Verified 2026-09-29 by live fetch of the landing page, summary and Chicago pages. Release dates verified against both the Fed's monthly calendar pages (newsevents/2026-MONTH.htm) and the Chicago Fed's data-release-calendar page: 2026-01-14, 03-04, 04-15, 06-03, 07-15, 09-02, 10-14, 11-25 (last two still ahead). Cadence is tagged monthly only for the freshness window (10 days); real cadence is 8 per year, so an unchanged item for 6 weeks is normal. Gotchas: not confirmed that the GitHub Actions runner IP can reach federalreserve.gov (worked from a residential IP); 2027 dates were not yet published (2027-january.htm is 404), re-check the calendar each December; returns [] if the landing page stops linking editions or the h4 headings change. Also weigh against: the Chicago Fed's National Activity Index is tracked as a calendar reminder in research_calendar.json.

sources.label: IPCC — News & Announcements
sources.notes: Added 2026-09-12 at the user's explicit request — treat as closely watched. Confirmed live: a real WordPress RSS feed (not the Reddit-digest source map's unrelated subreddit mention, which is a different, never-built feature and irrelevant here). IPCC's actual release cadence is irregular and multi-track, which is exactly why RSS (not a guessed calendar window) is the primary mechanism: as of this feed's live content, the AR7 (Seventh Assessment Report) cycle has its full multi-year timeline still UNRESOLVED — IPCC-63 (Oct 2025) and IPCC-64 (Mar 2026) both failed to agree a complete AR7 schedule (per Carbon Brief/ENB reporting), a genuinely unusual state of affairs. What IS confirmed and running: WGI's Second Lead Author Meeting (Apr 2026); WGI First Order Draft expert review open 10 Aug-2 Oct 2026 (active as of this writing); two Methodology Reports in progress for 2027 (Short-Lived Climate Forcers; Carbon Dioxide Removal/CCUS); a Special Report on Climate Change and Cities in final drafting. A handful of concrete near-term dates are in research_calendar.json's ipcc_ar7_milestones entry, but most of AR7 cannot be calendar-scheduled yet given the unresolved timeline — this weekly feed is the actual tracking mechanism, and should stay that way until (if ever) IPCC agrees a full AR7 schedule.

sources.label: Washington Center for Equitable Growth
sources.notes: Confirmed live 2026-09-12: real WordPress feed, posts near-daily (recent items on generative AI's labor-market effects, UI access gaps, housing wealth/political participation). Publishes far more often than monthly — treat as a monthly digest (summarize the most notable 2-4 posts from the past month, same convention as farmdoc_daily's weekly-digest treatment) rather than dumping every item.

sources.label: USDA Midwest Climate Hub
sources.notes: No hub-specific feed exists — .../hubs/midwest/feed and /rss.xml both 404 (confirmed 2026-09-12). The site-wide https://www.climatehubs.usda.gov/rss.xml (all ten regional Climate Hubs) is live and real, but most items are from other hubs (Northeast, Northwest, etc. — confirmed via live titles). Midwest items are sorted first via priority_keywords (changed 2026-09-22 from a keep_keyword_any filter at the user's request: priority, not exclusion, so a weekly run always has something). Non-Midwest hub items stay behind them.

sources.label: NOAA NCEI Monthly Climate Summary — Indiana/Michigan
sources.notes: Verified live 2026-09-15. One real bug found and fixed: combining datatypeid=[TAVG,TMAX,TMIN,PRCP] into a single request silently lost all temperature data — the CDO API's 1000-row cap was filling with precip-derived types (alphabetically ahead of T*) before temperature rows were reached, so only precip ever came back. Fixed by querying each datatype separately. Confirmed plausible output: Indiana/Michigan August 2026 avg temps (73.0°F / 68.0°F) and station-average precip, both consistent with the NCEI monthly report for the same period.

sources.label: USFS Forest Inventory and Analysis — Indiana (EVALIDator)
sources.notes: Verified live 2026-09-29, no API key. Uses the FIADB-API EVALIDator fullreport endpoint (JSON, outputFormat=NJSON); wc is the EVALID (18 + evaluation year; 182025 = Indiana's 2025 evaluation, annual panels 2019-2025). Reports forest land area, growing-stock volume, average annual mortality and net growth, plus mortality and growth as % of volume and the prior evaluation's mortality rate for comparison. First run: 14.07B cu ft, mortality 1.18%/yr (SE 5.5%), net growth 2.23%/yr; 2024 evaluation had mortality 1.19% — plausible and stable. GOTCHAS: (1) an unknown EVALID returns an HTML error page with HTTP 200, not JSON, so the scraper probes years downward from the current year (182026 currently does not exist). (2) The API gives no release date; item date is the end of the evaluation year, and the link carries #eval-<EVALID> so the history ledger adds exactly one entry per new annual evaluation and nothing on the daily runs between. (3) Only changes about once a year, so most Tuesday sessions will see the same item; the mortality SE (about 5%) is larger than year-to-year moves, so read the rate as a level, not a weekly signal. (4) This is an agency estimate table, not expert prose: there is no honest-null narrative to observe. It earns its place as a forest-health metric with a stated sampling error, the only forestry source that is quantitative. The annual USFS Forest Health Highlights PDFs remain a calendar entry in research_calendar.json.

sources.label: Midwestern Regional Climate Center — Monthly Climate Summary
sources.notes: Verified live 2026-09-29 by curl: RSS 2.0, 20 items, the latest being 'August 2026' (article #1756) with Midwest-average temperature (71.8F, +0.9F vs 1991-2020) and state-by-state departures written by MRCC climatologists (Purdue/NCEI partnership) — expert-synthesized, regional, and rarely in national news. Feed URL found via the RSS links on https://mrcc.purdue.edu/climatesummaries (there is no site-wide /rss or /feed; both 404). GOTCHAS: (1) pubDate is the START of the reported period (August 2026 shows Aug 1), not the posting date, so an item can look a month old the day it appears; the validator's freshness check uses fetched_at, so this does not trip it. (2) Sibling feeds exist at the same path with 'Weekly%20Summary', 'Quarterly%20Summary', 'Annual%20Summary' and 'ENSO%20Summary'. Weekly was NOT added: its newest item on 2026-09-29 was Sept 8-14, so it runs about two weeks behind and skips weeks, and it would crowd out the monthly synthesis. The Quarterly feed items are PDFs with image previews only (no text summary in the feed) and carry both Midwest and Great Lakes editions; revisit if the quarterly PDFs are wanted. (3) The feed summary is truncated to 300 characters by research_pull.py, which keeps the temperature paragraph but drops precipitation. Honest-null behavior not observed: every item examined reports numbers.

no_feed_available.note: Confirmed no usable RSS during setup (2026-09-12). US Drought Monitor, interconnection.fyi, and NASS Crop Progress now have direct scrapers/API integrations (type 'scrape' above). None currently outstanding.

sources.label: Aspen Institute — Financial Security Program
sources.reason: Cut 2026-09-29 at the maintainer's decision. Policy think tank; the usable feed is Aspen's site-wide one, filtered by keyword, and its items rarely carry a metric (4 items 09-08 to 09-14, empty since). The Fed distributional accounts cover the metric. The agent's standard review flagged it first; the maintainer judged it marketing-forward and low quality.

sources.label: Data Center Dynamics
sources.reason: Cut 2026-09-29 at the maintainer's decision. Trade news of deals and announcements, no expert-synthesized metric; the feed mixes in sponsored posts (about a fifth of ledger items carried sponsor/webinar markers) and unrelated telecom stories. Two low-value weeks were logged 09-15 and 09-22. Replacement candidates for the AI/grid-load question: EIA Electric Power Monthly (needs a free key) and MISO large-load data.

sources.label: Purdue Extension FNR — Got Nature? blog
sources.reason: Cut 2026-10-06 at the maintainer's decision: not valuable the way the ag and forestry data sources are. Extension blog, mostly educational posts with no metric (ID That Tree, license sales, Firewood Month); a few report observed Indiana conditions. The agent's standard review the same day put most of the feed outside the admission standard and asked for the maintainer's view. Its side role of surfacing Indiana Woodland Steward issues goes with it.

sources.label: drought.gov Midwest Drought Status Update
sources.reason: No structured API (Drupal site, no public JSON:API exposed). Worse, the update itself is irregular enough that no Midwest-specific update exists in the current listing at all (most recent regional updates were California-Nevada, Intermountain West, Southern Plains) — would mean building a scraper for content that isn't there most weeks. The drought_monitor source above already covers Indiana's drought classification directly from a real API, which is the higher-value, more reliable signal for the same underlying question.
